purpose: Bounded method evidence, not recipe findings or publication authorization.

sources.access: Relevant full page text read through web open.
sources.claim: Refrigerate seafood at 40°F or below when using within two days; otherwise freeze. Thaw overnight refrigerated, or sealed in cold water. Most seafood: 145°F; shrimp/scallops become firm, pearly and opaque. Perishables: maximum two hours unrefrigerated, one hour above 90°F.
sources.application: Fresh/thawed shrimp and scallops; distinguish cooking cue from elapsed-time guess. Keep raw-contact equipment separate from ready-to-eat garnishes.
sources.exclusion: Does not supply pan capacity, sear time, seafood count/size, or prove browning equals a cooked center.

editorialChecksNotSourceClaims: Record thawing dependency, seafood size, drying, pan dimensions and number of batches. Measure whole elapsed time including sauce/garnish work and reheating between batches.
Assess interior endpoint separately from surface sear. Count all separate ingredient uses and raw-contact sauce paths.
unknowns: No additional primary searing mechanism source verified within this bounded packet; drying/crowding effects and exact batch capacity remain questions for source review or cooking tests.
limits: No recipe-specific blind-reference findings used. No kitchen test. Quantities, yields, safety changes and identity changes require exception review.
